Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Ιουλίου, «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος», with the rank word left off.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 12 iulie — «Sfântul Mucenic Proclu»

attestations.note: The day prints the two men on separate lines, each with its own copy of one shared life, so the corpus keeps one folder for each. The life itself dates Hilary's death to 15 July, three days after Proclus's, and the Romanian calendar keeps them both on 12 iulie.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the Greek line pairs the same two men the Romanian one does — «Sfântul Mucenic Proclu» and «Sfântul Mucenic Ilarie» against «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος». The pairing and the day settle him against the corpus's five other men of the name. The Greek page adds the reign the Romanian did not — the emperor Trajan, which it brackets 98 to 117, and the governor Maximus — and the manner of his death, the arrows. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints two apolytikia: the first names both men and is taken, and the second is the common of several martyrs «Οἱ Μάρτυρες σου Κύριε», printed under their name, which is taken as a common and said here to be one.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Proclu și Ilarie», Glasul 4 — the common troparion of martyrs, printed here for the two of them; the spelling «nesctricăciunii» is the page's own

english.text: Your martyrs, Lord, in their struggles received from You, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Your strength they overthrew their torturers and broke the powerless insolence of the demons. At their prayers, Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Σταυροῦ τὴν πανοπλίαν ἱερῶς ἐνδυσάμενοι, Ἰλάριε καὶ Πρόκλε, ὑπὲρ φύσιν ἠθλήσατε, καὶ δόξης οὐρανίου κοινωνοί, ἐδείχθητε ὡς μέτοχοι Χριστοῦ, διὰ τοῦτο χαρισμάτων ταὶς δωρεαίς, πυρσεύετε τοὺς κράζοντας, δόξα τῷ ἐνισχύσαντι ὑμᾶς, δόξα τῷ στεφανώοαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι δι' ὑμῶν πάσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος ἀ’, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the first of two apolytikia on the shared page of «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος», and it names them both

english.text: Having sacredly put on the full armour of the Cross, Hilary and Proclus, you contended beyond nature, and were shown sharers of heavenly glory as partakers of Christ; and so by the gifts of your graces you set alight those who cry: Glory to him who strengthened you, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who works healings for all through you.

hymns.text: Οἱ Μάρτυρες σου Κύριε, ἐν τῇ ἀθλήσει αὐτῶν, τὸ στέφος ἐκομίσαντο τῆς ἀφθαρσίας, ἐκ σοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν· σχόντες γὰρ τὴν ἰσχύν σου, τοὺς τυράννους καθεῖλον· ἔθραυσαν καὶ δαιμόνων τὰ ἀνίσχυρα θράση. Αὐτῶν ταῖς ἱκεσίαις Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, σῶσον τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε — the second apolytikion on the shared page of the two. It is the common of several martyrs, printed under their name and naming nobody else, and is copied as the page has it

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their contending received from you our God the crown of incorruption; for having your strength they brought down the tyrants, and shattered the powerless insolence of the demons. By their entreaties, Christ our God, save our souls.
